title: Type the catch/catchError clauses across sync_orchestrator.dart, pull_pipeline.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart (EH-4)
why: All 16 sites catch without an `on <Type>` clause, so each also catches Error subtypes (TypeError, StateError, RangeError, NoSuchMethodError) as if they were the transient I/O failures the surrounding code is designed to shrug off. Every one of these swallows-and-logs (the pull_pipeline.dart and tutored_listener_supervisor.dart sites don't rethrow at all; most of the sync_orchestrator.dart sites log a warning and return/fall through). Concrete cost: if a future change introduces a null-dereference or bad cast inside a merger reached from the 60s periodic drain, a recovery-pull trigger, or a listener dispatch, it gets caught here, logged once per occurrence as an ordinary 'drain failed'/'listener error' warning, and never crashes or reaches Crashlytics as a fatal -- masking a real regression indefinitely instead of surfacing it. (Two other sites -- sync_orchestrator.dart:768 and :939 -- were deliberately excluded from this list: :768 delegates to a typed `_isLocalDatabaseError` classifier before deciding to swallow, and :939 rethrows after converting to a status; both already behave like the fix this finding asks for elsewhere.)
recommendation: Narrow each listed catch to `on Exception catch` (Exception still covers FirebaseException/TimeoutException/SocketException etc.) so Error subtypes propagate to the zone's uncaught-error handler instead of being absorbed; use sync_orchestrator.dart:768's classifier-based pattern as the template for guards that need to stay broad on purpose.
acceptance_criteria: Enable avoid_catches_without_on_clauses + avoid_catching_errors once dart run custom_lint is unblocked; all 16 sites pass.
A test that injects a StateError into a merger/dispatch call reached from one of these paths shows the error propagating (not silently logged-and-continued).
